title: When Pain and Anguish Seize Me, Lord
description: When Pain and Anguish Seize Me, Lord in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 119, part 17, headed “Courage and perseverance under persecution; or, Grace shining in difficulties and trials”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When pain and an-guish seize me, Lord, All my sup-port is from thy word: My soul dis-solves for heav-i-ness, Up-hold me with thy strength-ening grace.

lines: When pain and anguish seize me, Lord,
All my support is from thy word:
Uphold me with thy strengthening grace.
The proud have fram'd their scoffs and lies,
They watch my feet with envious eyes,
And tempt my soul to snares and sin,
Yet thy commands I ne'er decline.
They hate me, Lord, without a cause,
They hate to see me love thy laws:
But I will trust and fear thy Name,
Till pride and malice die with shame.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
